turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome in! What can I do for you today?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Morning. Um, well, I've just moved house, and I'd really love to join the library, if that's possible.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Of course, that's no trouble at all. Lovely to have you. How are you finding the move? It's a bit grey out there this morning, isn't it? I nearly came in without a coat, and then of course it started drizzling.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, it's been quite a change, honestly. Lots of boxes still sitting in the hallway, and I can't find the kettle anywhere. But everyone has been really friendly so far. The lady next door even brought round a cake, which was very kind, and the children have already found the park.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ah, the kettle is always the very last thing you find. Right, let's get you sorted. I'll pull up the application on the screen here. Could I take your surname first, please?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, of course. It's Whitlock, just like it sounds.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Whitlock, lovely, thank you. Funny, we had a Whitlock who used to run the Saturday story club here, years ago. Anyway, I'll need your birthday for the system, just the day and the month.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, right, yes. It's the 17th of September.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Sorry, did you say the 70th? I might have misheard that.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No, no, nothing like that. Nearly the middle of the month, as it happens.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Got it, thanks very much. Now, your address. What number are you on the road?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's 58. Um, sorry, no, it's 48. I keep getting it wrong, because I've only just learned it myself and the old flat had a completely different number.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: No worries at all, I still muddle my own postcode some days. And what's the name of the road?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's Wrenfield Road, that's W-R-E-N-F-I-E-L-D, and then just Road.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Wrenfield, perfect, I know it. It runs up past the bakery and the little park, doesn't it? And what's the place called, so I get the postcode right?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Penhallow, that's P-E-N-H-A-L-L-O-W. It's a small place, so people usually guess it wrong.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right, I've got that down. And have you lived in this part of the country for long, or is it all new to you?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, quite a while, actually. We've lived in this part of the country for 14 years now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Sorry, was that 40?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ha, no, 14! I'm not quite that old. We just fancied a bigger garden, that's all.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ah, a garden, how nice. And which city were you living in just before you moved over here?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Well, it was Ellesford, that's E-L-L-E-S-F-O-R-D, about forty minutes down the road.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I know Ellesford, it has a lovely market. Right, we're nearly there. Your card takes a few days to print, so when would suit you to pop in and collect it?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Um, let me think. Thursday would be best, because it's my day off.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Perfect, I'll make a note of that. Do bring along something with your new address on, like a bill or a bank letter, when you come. We have a few libraries around the borough, so which one will you mostly be using?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The one down by the river, Riverside, since it's right on my walk to work.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good choice, it has the café too, and the children's corner has just been repainted. It's very popular on rainy afternoons. And one last thing, just for our records. How did you find out about the library?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It was in the school newsletter that came home in my daughter's bag, not the council one.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Brilliant, that's everything I need. You can borrow up to 12 items at a time, which is plenty for most people, and renewing is easy online if you get behind. We'll pop you a message when the card is ready.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Wonderful, thank you so much. You've been really helpful, and I'm glad I came in before the weekend. My daughter will be thrilled, she reads everything. See you on the day!

evidence.quote: It's Whitlock, just like it sounds.
It's Wrenfield Road, that's W-R-E-N-F-I-E-L-D, and then just Road.
We've lived in this part of the country for 14 years now.
Well, it was Ellesford, that's E-L-L-E-S-F-O-R-D, about forty minutes down the road.
Thursday would be best, because it's my day off.
The one down by the river, Riverside, since it's right on my walk to work.
It was in the school newsletter that came home in my daughter's bag, not the council one.
